active_paradigms.idea: Optimize the squared-distance feasibility problem directly with scipy.optimize.minimize(method='trust-constr') using nonlinear constraints d(i,j)^2 >= t and d(i,j)^2 <= 1, maximizing t as an extra variable.
active_paradigms.description: Reformulate exactly as the evaluator hints: variables are the 42 point coordinates plus t; constraints are 91 lower bounds d^2 - t >= 0 and 91 upper bounds 1 - d^2 >= 0, all smooth quadratics with analytic Jacobians. Use scipy.optimize.minimize with method='trust-constr', minimizing -t, supplying NonlinearConstraint objects with vectorized constraint functions and precomputed sparse Jacobians (each constraint involves only 6 coordinates). Warm-start from the current best configuration (which already achieves ratio ~0.4898) and from structured seeds. Because trust-constr handles the KKT conditions of the true feasibility NLP, it can push t past what penalty-based L-BFGS homotopy reaches, since penalty methods leave a small feasibility gap. Increase t incrementally (t += 1e-5) re-solving each time, an exact feasible ascent on the certified lower bound. Guard with time checks and return the best feasible configuration normalized to unit diameter.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: primary combined_score = (dmin/dmax)^2 / benchmark; directly maximizes the certified lower bound t
active_paradigms.cautions: Provide analytic Jacobians (2*(xi-xj) pattern) and use sparse LinearConstraint-style sparsity via NonlinearConstraint with jac returning sparse matrices for speed; verify final feasibility numerically (all distances in [t,1]-1e-9) before returning; keep total runtime under the timeout by limiting major iterations per t-step.

active_paradigms.idea: Simulated annealing / basin-hopping on the exact ratio objective using scipy.optimize.basinhopping with a min-max aware step generator.
active_paradigms.description: Use scipy.optimize.basinhopping on the objective f(p) = -(dmin/dmax) with a custom take_step that moves the point participating in the currently shortest or longest edge along the pair direction (the gradient-informative directions), plus occasional random rotations of the whole configuration (invariance-aware moves that don't change the objective but help escape basins when combined with perturbation). Each basin-hopping iteration locally minimizes with L-BFGS-B on a smooth surrogate: maximize sum of softmin distances, e.g. objective -logsumexp(-d/eps) combined with diameter penalty, which approximates the true nonsmooth ratio well for small eps. Run multiple seeds including the known good structured seeds (icosahedron+2 poles, double hexagon rings). The key difference from the current hill-climb is acceptance of worsening moves (Metropolis) enabling escape from the local optimum at ratio ~0.4898.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: primary (dmin/dmax)^2 via the smooth surrogate and exact ratio evaluation at the end
active_paradigms.cautions: The true ratio is nonsmooth; always do final local polish on the exact ratio; set temperature adaptively (accept ~20-30%); use fixed seed; enforce time budget by capping niter based on elapsed time per iteration.

active_paradigms.idea: Exploit graph/geometric structure: parameterize candidate 14-point configurations by distance-graph topology and search over contact graphs with a force-balance (Stress majorization / spectral) solver.
active_paradigms.description: At the optimum, the shortest and longest distances form contact graphs. Enumerate plausible topologies: e.g., 14 vertices as two staggered hexagonal rings plus 2 poles (best known candidates), or icosahedron-based capsid structures. For a hypothesized graph with prescribed edge lengths all equal to 1 (both min and max contacts at 1), solve the graph realization / stress equilibrium: find coordinates where each vertex is in equilibrium under unit forces along its contact edges (a first-order condition of the optimum). Implement as fixed-point iteration: each point moves to the weighted centroid of its graph neighbors (stress majorization à la scipy-free implementation, or use scipy.sparse.linalg.eigs on the stress matrix). Then verify and hill-climb. Additionally try spectral placement: use the eigenvectors of the contact-graph Laplacian as initial 3D embedding, then refine. This explores fundamentally different geometric structures than random repulsion seeds.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: primary score by discovering a better contact topology than the current best local optimum
active_paradigms.cautions: Graph realization may not exist for a hypothesized topology; check all pairwise distances and discard infeasible realizations; keep several topologies within time budget; use fixed seeds for any randomized refinement.
